items.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
items.text: Reorder dashboard variables: Authors can now reorder dashboard variables directly in the dashboard editor. See Use dashboard variables. Display names for field variable options: Authors can now set a display name for each option in a field variable, such as Total revenue instead of Sum of sales. You can also ask Genie Code to set, rename, or clear these display names, and it keeps the names you set when it edits the variable. See Set display names for field options. Import relationships from Unity Catalog with Genie Code (Beta): Genie Code for dashboard authoring can now import the relationships declared on Unity Catalog metric views into a dashboard as dashboard relationships. See Use relationships with Genie Code for dashboard authoring. Waterfall chart labels: Labels on waterfall charts now stay visible when they're close to the top or bottom of the axis.

items.title: AI Functions require Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS or above
items.text: Beginning in January 2027, AI Functions that require Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above, other than ai_similarity, require Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS or above. Calls to these functions on Databricks Runtime versions below 17.3 are no longer supported and return an error. Upgrade the compute that runs affected SQL queries to Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS or above before support ends. This change does not affect the AI Functions REST API. See Transform unstructured data using AI Functions.

items.title: AI Function tasks for jobs (Beta)
items.text: You can now add AI Function tasks to your Azure Databricks jobs to run ai_parse_document, ai_extract, or ai_classify on the files in a volume or the rows of a table, without writing SQL. Each run processes only the inputs that are new or changed since the previous run and writes the results to a Unity Catalog table that later tasks can read. This feature is in Beta. See AI Function tasks for jobs.

items.title: Build more connected workflows with Fabric Actions and Business Actions in Fabric Pipelines (Preview)
items.text: Sections: Bring Fabric operations directly into your pipelines; Connect your pipelines to more business applications; Find and configure the action you need; Discover Fabric operations; Configure your action; Go from data workflows to business workflows; More actions, more possibilities; Get started. Modern data workflows rarely stop at moving and transforming data. Once data is ready, you may need to trigger another operation in Fabric, refresh a semantic model, update a business application, send a notification, generate a document, or kick off the next step in a business process. With Fabric Actions and Business Actions activities in Microsoft Fabric Data Factory, you can bring these steps directly into your Fabric pipelines. Together, these activities make it easier to orchestrate workflows across Fabric and the business applications your organization relies on, without having to build and maintain custom API integrations for every scenario. items.title: Regular expression functions in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.text: Sections: What’s new in preview; Extract useful values from raw text; Validate contact data before it reaches downstream systems; Conclusion. Data warehouses routinely ingest valuable information embedded in free text, where inconsistent structure makes it difficult to query, connect, and analyze. Incoming values can also require quality checks before they reach curated tables. Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint now support scalar regular expression functions in preview, so you can extract useful values, validate formats, standardize text, and mask sensitive data directly in T-SQL instead of adding a separate processing step. Regular expressions provide a concise way to recognize, extract, and transform complex text patterns that would otherwise require multiple string operations.
